answer: Each identity claims one basalt bridge pier, locking a 90-credit bond. Its fee rises with the funder's pier count: first 28, kth 28+8(k-1), 1,000th 8,020, 1,000 piers 4,024,000 in fees plus 90,000 locked. The keeper posts a zephyr log of wind speed, load, and sway; an auditor recomputes pier load from the basalt bridge table, and a reused pier serial or mismatched load burns the bond. A rented-pier ring fails because a pier serial is key-bound to one keeper, so a second log under it burns both bonds. An honest keeper pays 28 once and recovers the bond after audit.
